[h1]Dora-The-Explorer Word Puzzles, Platforming That Feels Like Molasses, and as Much Story as LaCroix Has Flavour[/h1]

Gosh, I really wanted to like and recommend this one, but it just flops. I'm kind of baffled by the high reviews and number of awards it's won when it offers so little value to the player. At the time I'm writing this, less than half of players have the achievement for completing the first chapter, and it's not at all surprising that it doesn't take most people much time to drop this game.

I'm not sure what the main gameplay appeal of this game is meant to be. It's a mix between word puzzles and platforming, but it's barely passable at the former, flat-out bad at the latter, and chooses to lean more heavily on the one it does a worse job of.

The word puzzles are rarely interesting enough to justify building a game around them. Most of them just involve retrieving the letters you need to spell an obvious word, which means they're actually platforming challenges rather than word puzzles. The tense/climactic moments in the game, including [spoiler]the final boss battle[/spoiler], also all rely far more on the platforming than the word mechanics. Unfortunately, the platforming that the gameplay relies so much on is clunky, slow, and awkward. Moving around to get anything done in this game feels like work rather than play. 

Lastly, the narrative. It seems to be about a hero who is good fighting ambiguous oppressors who are bad, and by reading this sentence you now know as much about the plot of this game as you would learn by playing the entire game. This wouldn't necessarily be a huge issue for the game if the gameplay were good. But it isn't.

[h2]Very short, but VERY unique puzzle platformer![/h2]

Okay so, storytime. This is a [i]Wii U[/i] game. At least originally. Made some pretty neat use of the gamepad there too, what with being able to use the touchscreen as your keyboard to type in or rearrange words!

Anyway it absolutely [b]bombed[/b] there for obvious reasons. It was an indie on Wii U, it was never going to sell much there.
So a year or so after that they came up with this [i]"Revised"[/i] version, which slightly touches up some elements of it (graphics and audio and such), and axes the gamepad features in favor of a more generalist implementation of the mechanics where the keyboard just pops up on screen and you use it with regular buttons.
A bit of a sad loss since it's SO MUCH SLOWER than touch inputs, but fair enough. Guess they needed a way to be able to port the game to other systems without that hardware feature.


Anyway! The game itself.
It's a VERY simple linear cinematic 2D platformer, think something along the lines of Limbo, but with an emphasis on words and their power. Taken literally, in this case, since a good portion of the environmental elements as well as every single living entity is made up of words. Namely, one single word come to life or having some effect around itself in some way.

It's a very [i]unique[/i] setup, one that I've definitely never seen done elsewhere.
So, the main gimmick of this game plays around those [b]words[/b]. Every single puzzle revolves around them. You'll have to make up words, or rearrange letters into words that you need, all so that you can do SOMETHING on the environment to progress.

For example, say, a mechanism that's turned off, so you find the letters to put together the word "ON" which turns on every mechanism in a big radius around itself. Or you need to open a door so you make "OPEN". Or you need to move a platform so you make "RAISE", or "MOVE", or something along those lines. You get the point, it basically all revolves around that.

There's harmful words that you'll have to avoid, or modify in some way, or use LIEs (an entity that can invert words to their antonyms) to turn them into good words. Or use good words to begin with to protect yourself against them, since such words can give you a protective shield if you stick close to them.


Genuinely? 
I LOVE this game's ideas and what it does with them.

The visuals are super pretty and hand-drawn (even if the characters use "puppet" animation which can feel a bit cheap, but I feel it works for critters made of letters like this). The sound design is WONDERFULLY atmospheric, especially if you're using headphones.
There's even a couple of minigame modes for extra content!


But really, I think this game's main problem (which it was criticized for even back on Wii U) is its [b]length[/b]. It's three chapters, and can be beat in a couple hours TOPS if you're exploring a lot for the side collectibles and having a really hard time with the puzzles. It's a shame, because by the time the game feels like it's picking up it just... ENDS, unceremoniously. You beat the boss, yipee, you win. Roll credits.

And it's a shame! Because, again, I love this game and everything it's going for! It just kind of feels like it doesn't get to do EVERYTHING it could've done with its ideas because of how quickly it's over...

Though I guess for a $10 game it's fine? Especially when it goes on sale often, I think I got this game for like $2 a couple years back. It goes for SUPER cheap, and honestly at that point it's worth it just to experience the novelty of the super cool ideas they had here.


[b]TLDR:[/b] Very short puzzler, but with a VERY unique mechanic that's used super well (for as little as it lasts). Very much worth playing just for the experience, at least on sale.

[h1]Typoman —— 字母人[/h1]
眼前一亮的解谜游戏

+独特的拼单词解谜
（排列字母拼出合适的单词，解开谜题闯过难关，很独特的体验。开头的Crush变成Rush就很有巧思，后期的LIE设计更是神来之笔）
+细节打磨到位
（游戏用字母置景很有氛围感。制作组给不少单词做了互动效果，保证了玩家不会因为在选词方面对不上电波而卡关，还给不少单词做了彩蛋效果，给热爱头脑风暴拼单词的你足够的正反馈）

+-对玩家的英语水平有基础要求
（游戏过程中用到的单词并不难，但依然不适合用来学英语，游戏没有做学习系统或者提示设计，词汇量不达标还是会卡关，更推荐那些还没有被大学生活抚平大脑褶皱的高三毕业生来玩）

-操作设计不方便，成就设置不太友好
（基于手柄做的操作逻辑，选字母不太方便。专门做成就的时间数倍于通关时间，做不开单词板通关成就的我就像个扛着巨石的苦行僧，限制死亡次数的成就让那些极限跳跃的关卡变得面目可憎，迷你游戏拼单词更是有足足165个，做到1/3时就倍感疲倦，还是选择开着单词本抄作业）

独特的设计和体验，值得一玩

알파벳을 조합하여 단어를 만들고, 그 단어의 효과로 길을 열어나가는 퍼즐플랫폼게임입니다. 중간중간 점프액션 구간이 있구요. 독특한 아이디어에 적당한 난이도와 플레이타임으로 가볍게 즐기기 좋았습니다. 엔딩 후 미니게임 두 가지 제공해주는 것도 재밌었구요. 

 주어진 알파벳만을 사용해 단어를 만들어야 하기 때문에 어떤 단어로 조합할지 궁리하는 재미가 좋았습니다. 퍼뜩 떠오른 단어가 있어도 주어진 알파벳으로는 못 만드는 경우가 많아서, 어떤 단어로 어떤 효과를 내야 하는지 이것저것 시도해보게 되네요. 게임 진행에 필요한 효과가 있는 단어들뿐만 아니라 화면 이펙트라거나 주인공의 외양 등에 변화를 주는 단어들도 있고, 즉사 처리를 해버리는 등의 부정적인 효과도 있어서, 이것저것 단어를 만들어 어떻게 되는지 보는 재미도 좋았습니다. 

 다만 게임 구조상 약간의 영단어 지식이 필요하기에, 비영어권 플레이어에겐 재미를 느끼는 데 접근성을 해치는 난점으로 작용될 듯합니다. 사용되는 단어들이 그렇게까지 어려운 단어들은 아니지만, 그냥 영어 단어를 사용한다는 점에서 거부감이 느껴질 수도 있구요. 몇몇 단어는 사전을 찾아봐야 했고, Lie 단어를 사용해 반대말로 철자를 바꾸는 기믹도 있어서, 영어에 익숙치 않다면 좀처럼 손이 가질 않을 게임입니다.

Typoman est un jeu de plateforme et de réflexion qui se démarque par son concept original basé sur les mots et les lettres. L'un des aspects les plus intéressants de Typoman est son utilisation créative du langage et de la littérature pour résoudre des énigmes et progresser dans le jeu. Les joueurs contrôlent un personnage composé de lettres qui peuvent être manipulées pour former différents mots et déclencher des actions dans le monde du jeu.

 Typoman propose un concept de jeu original en utilisant les mots et les lettres comme mécanique centrale. Les joueurs doivent manipuler les lettres pour former des mots qui ont un impact direct sur le monde du jeu, ce qui offre une expérience de jeu unique et créative.Le jeu présente des énigmes stimulantes et ingénieuses qui exigent une réflexion et une compréhension du langage. Les joueurs doivent parfois trouver des mots spécifiques pour résoudre des obstacles ou progresser dans l'histoire, ce qui ajoute une dimension intellectuelle au gameplay. Le jeu aborde des thèmes profonds et évocateurs, tels que le pouvoir des mots et la lutte contre les forces obscures de la négligence et de la corruption. Cette dimension thématique donne une profondeur supplémentaire à l'expérience de jeu. 

Cependant, Le concept de jeu basé sur les mots peut être déroutant pour certains joueurs qui préfèrent des mécaniques de jeu plus traditionnelles. La nécessité de comprendre et de manipuler le langage peut rendre le jeu moins accessible pour ceux qui recherchent une expérience de jeu plus directe ou plus action. Bien que les énigmes dans Typoman soient intéressantes et stimulantes, certains joueurs pourraient trouver qu'elles deviennent répétitives au fil du jeu. La mécanique centrale basée sur les mots peut limiter la variété des défis que les joueurs rencontrent. Typoman peut parfois manquer de variété dans ses environnements de jeu. Les décors et les zones peuvent sembler relativement similaires tout au long du jeu, ce qui pourrait rendre l'exploration moins captivante pour certains joueurs.  Étant donné que Typoman repose sur la manipulation des mots et du langage, il peut être moins accessible aux joueurs qui ne maîtrisent pas bien la langue dans laquelle le jeu est présenté (Anglais). Cela pourrait limiter son attrait pour les joueurs non natifs de la langue du jeu. Le temps de jeux assez court peut aussi repoussé les joueurs à l'achat de celui ci.
